simple.meaning: מָזִיחַ (mâzîyach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a belt (as movable).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Job, Psalms, Isaiah, beginning at Job 12:21. Its contexts include family line, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מָזִיחַ (H4206).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.full: H4206. maziyach מֵ֫זַח noun masculine girdle (according to Bondi 11 WMM As.u.Eur.104 loan-word from Egypt mdµ , compare Lag GGN 1889, 310 ); — absolute ׳מ : — in simile of curse enfolding the wicked Psa 109:19 (|| בֶּגֶד ); figurative = restraint Isa 23:10 (but text dubious). [ מְזִיחַ ] noun masculine id. (of like origin): — only construct ׳מ רִמָּה אֲפִיקִים Job 12:21 loosen the girdle of mighty ; i.e. weaken them, make them defenceless, by ungirding. מַזְכִּיר see זכר . hiphil

occurrences.englishText: Let it be to him as the clothing with which he covers himself,
Pass through your land like the Nile, daughter of Tarshish. There is no restraint any more.
